I think this is a very fair point. For myself, I've adopted the following strategy: (1) turn off all Windows updating functionality, including permanently disabling the Windows Update service using the Task Manager; (2) learn more about exactly what Windows 10 is doing, and what the security benefits of moving to Linux would be; (3) find out how easy it will be to move to Linux; (4) examine hardware requirements, and decide if it's time to upgrade my machines anyway; (5) if the benefits outweigh the disadvantages, make the move.

I would strongly advise you consider using it on VirtualBox first. VirtualBox is pretty well-supported by most major Linux distributions, and using it can give you an idea on what to expect when you try it on your machine as a main operating system. I would also consider using a LiveCD and trying it out that way - actually try several distros out that way so you can see what you like.

Don't worry TOO much about upgrading your hardware. An unfortunate reality with Linux is that brand new devices often do not have optimal support, because drivers have to be modified (or in extreme cases written from scratch), which necessarily takes time. If you do upgrade, be sure to make sure you get something you know is Linux compatible. Some things are, some things aren't. That said, good on you for taking some initiative here.
